blocks.text: Dohra:

The Singhs were neither scared of being killed (in the battle), Nor did they expect any support of reinforcements from anywhere. (So) in whatever direction they advanced and headed their attack, They went on a killing spree in that self same direction. (1)
lines: The Singhs were neither scared of being killed (in the battle),
Nor did they expect any support of reinforcements from anywhere.
(So) in whatever direction they advanced and headed their attack,
They went on a killing spree in that self same direction.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Now let me describe the situation as it prevailed on the other front, Towards which the Mughal forces had proceeded. They had rushed posthaste towards (Banda Singh's fort) in gay abandon, As if a rich feast had been laid out for them there. (2)
lines: Now let me describe the situation as it prevailed on the other front,
Towards which the Mughal forces had proceeded.
They had rushed posthaste towards (Banda Singh's fort) in gay abandon,
As if a rich feast had been laid out for them there.

blocks.text: Both the walls and the domes of (Banda Singh's fort) hd been demolished, By the continuous pounding by the Mughal's canon fire. Though this demolition created gaping holes for the entry of Mughal forces, Still many step ladders were placed for climbing up into the fort. (3)
lines: Both the walls and the domes of (Banda Singh's fort) hd been demolished,
By the continuous pounding by the Mughal's canon fire.
Though this demolition created gaping holes for the entry of Mughal forces,
Still many step ladders were placed for climbing up into the fort.

blocks.text: In this manner, some Mughal troops entered into the fort, Who were encountered by the Singhs entrenched inside. While some Singhs thought of pleading before Banda Singh for help, Others thought that that was not an opportune moment for pleadings. (4)
lines: In this manner, some Mughal troops entered into the fort,
Who were encountered by the Singhs entrenched inside.
While some Singhs thought of pleading before Banda Singh for help,
Others thought that that was not an opportune moment for pleadings.

blocks.text: In case they deserted the field and fell at Banda Singh's feet, They would never be pardoned and accepted in the Divine Court,
This was a moment to fight and die for a cause, Rather than a moment for begging for protection (from Banda Singh). (5)
lines: This was a moment to fight and die for a cause,
Rather than a moment for begging for protection (from Banda Singh).

blocks.text: When a leader of an organisation himself comes under a grave threat, It does not behove his martial followers to choose a path of appeals. Those who sacrifice their lives for the sake of their leader, They become worthy of Divine grace and happiness in heaven. (6)
lines: When a leader of an organisation himself comes under a grave threat,
It does not behove his martial followers to choose a path of appeals.
Those who sacrifice their lives for the sake of their leader,
They become worthy of Divine grace and happiness in heaven.

blocks.text: Dohra:

This was a moment to fight and make sacrifices, Rather than a moment to make appeals for protection. Those who happened to survive this moment of crises, They would have every right to make appeals for further safety. (7)
lines: This was a moment to fight and make sacrifices,
Rather than a moment to make appeals for protection.
Those who happened to survive this moment of crises,
They would have every right to make appeals for further safety.

blocks.text: Then the Singhs, mustering their courage and will power, Killed all those Mughal soldiers who dared to enter the fort. (Dear readers) listen further to the account of all those, Who managed to climb up the fort walls (with step ladders). (8)
lines: Then the Singhs, mustering their courage and will power,
Killed all those Mughal soldiers who dared to enter the fort.
(Dear readers) listen further to the account of all those,
Who managed to climb up the fort walls (with step ladders).

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Those who caught the roof tops after climbing up the stairs, They got their hands chopped off (By the Singh's swords). While they fell down on the ground from the rooftops, Listen about those who were standing outside the fort. (9)
lines: Those who caught the roof tops after climbing up the stairs,
They got their hands chopped off (By the Singh's swords).
While they fell down on the ground from the rooftops,
Listen about those who were standing outside the fort.

blocks.text: Although they approached the doors in batches and contingents, Some of them beat a (hasty) retreat while others hesitated to enter. Volley of bullets came with a stunning velocity from inside, Along with the hissing sound of arrows shot from the bows. (10)
lines: Although they approached the doors in batches and contingents,
Some of them beat a (hasty) retreat while others hesitated to enter.
Volley of bullets came with a stunning velocity from inside,
Along with the hissing sound of arrows shot from the bows.

blocks.text: Some Singh soldiers stood inside with drawn out swords in hands, Who engaged (the intruding) Mughals in a direct fight? As the muskets fired bullets from both the sides, There were piles of corpses heaped up at the entry points. (11)
lines: Some Singh soldiers stood inside with drawn out swords in hands,
Who engaged (the intruding) Mughals in a direct fight?
As the muskets fired bullets from both the sides,
There were piles of corpses heaped up at the entry points.

blocks.text: Such a heavy pall of din, dust and smoke hung over the place, That it became difficult to distinguish between friend and foe. The bodies from both the sides were so inextricably mixed up, That everyone lost his identity in this blinding chaos. (12)
lines: Such a heavy pall of din, dust and smoke hung over the place,
That it became difficult to distinguish between friend and foe.
The bodies from both the sides were so inextricably mixed up,
That everyone lost his identity in this blinding chaos.

blocks.text: Dohra:

While those in the rear butchered those in the front, Nobody could make a distinction (between friend and foe). As a comrades-in-arms started killing their own fraternal colleagues, An extremely fierce battle ensued at the sight. (13)
lines: While those in the rear butchered those in the front,
Nobody could make a distinction (between friend and foe).
As a comrades-in-arms started killing their own fraternal colleagues,
An extremely fierce battle ensued at the sight.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Corpses were piled upon each other in such a heap, As if a wall was being built with these dead bodies. It appeared as if a merchant had arrived with his cargo, And piled up his merchandise in a heap of bags. (14)
lines: Corpses were piled upon each other in such a heap,
As if a wall was being built with these dead bodies.
It appeared as if a merchant had arrived with his cargo,
And piled up his merchandise in a heap of bags.

blocks.text: Bodies of dead horses were heaped upon each other, As if a woodcutter had chopped off trunks of huge trees. The severed heads of soldiers were lying scattered in the fields, As if a farmer had ploughed through a field of melons. (15)
lines: Bodies of dead horses were heaped upon each other,
As if a woodcutter had chopped off trunks of huge trees.
The severed heads of soldiers were lying scattered in the fields,
As if a farmer had ploughed through a field of melons.

blocks.text: Streams of blood started flowing in such abundance, As if a water channel flowed to irrigate an orchard. The whole earth got splattered with the red blood, As if the soldiers' dresses were dyed in red colour. (16)
lines: Streams of blood started flowing in such abundance,
As if a water channel flowed to irrigate an orchard.
The whole earth got splattered with the red blood,
As if the soldiers' dresses were dyed in red colour.

blocks.text: The fort doors were blocked with dead bodies in such a way, As if these doors were given a coat of red painting very recently. From whatever side the Mughals soldiers tried to sneak in, The Singhs rushed in the same direction to counter them. (17)
lines: The fort doors were blocked with dead bodies in such a way,
As if these doors were given a coat of red painting very recently.
From whatever side the Mughals soldiers tried to sneak in,
The Singhs rushed in the same direction to counter them.

blocks.text: Dohra:

While the Mughals rushed from a distance to launch an attack, The Singhs repulsed their attack when they came near. While the Singhs faced death by rushing forward, The Mughals died while beating a (hasty) retreat. (18)
lines: While the Mughals rushed from a distance to launch an attack,
The Singhs repulsed their attack when they came near.
While the Singhs faced death by rushing forward,
The Mughals died while beating a (hasty) retreat.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Since the Singhs were too keen to make a sacrifice, They decided to make a virtue out of necessity. The Singhs, having lost all hopes of saving their lives, Prepared themselves (mentally) to sacrifice their lives. (19)
lines: Since the Singhs were too keen to make a sacrifice,
They decided to make a virtue out of necessity.
The Singhs, having lost all hopes of saving their lives,
Prepared themselves (mentally) to sacrifice their lives.

blocks.text: Paying little attention to the pain of their bodily wounds, The Singhs wielded their weapons with a death wish in their hearts. Since the Mughals had invaded with the aim of plundering, They had to face such an ordeal (at the hands of committed Singhs). (20)
lines: Paying little attention to the pain of their bodily wounds,
The Singhs wielded their weapons with a death wish in their hearts.
Since the Mughals had invaded with the aim of plundering,
They had to face such an ordeal (at the hands of committed Singhs).

blocks.text: The Mughals found the Singhs blocking their passage in every direction, And noticed every single Singh fighting against ten Mughal soldiers. The Singhs were found jumping over the fort walls, And attacking the Mughal soldiers without retreating a bit. (21)
lines: The Mughals found the Singhs blocking their passage in every direction,
And noticed every single Singh fighting against ten Mughal soldiers.
The Singhs were found jumping over the fort walls,
And attacking the Mughal soldiers without retreating a bit.

blocks.text: Whichever Mughal soldier survived, he beat a hasty retreat, Such was the mood of the battle that ensued there. Corpses were piled upon corpses in such a manner, As if bags used for loading a mule were piled upon each other. (22)
lines: Whichever Mughal soldier survived, he beat a hasty retreat,
Such was the mood of the battle that ensued there.
Corpses were piled upon corpses in such a manner,
As if bags used for loading a mule were piled upon each other.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Whenever a Mughal soldier got wounded in the battle, His four other companions rushed backwards towards the cover. While two among those four pretended to pick up the wounded, The other two followed the first two without any reason. (23)
lines: Whenever a Mughal soldier got wounded in the battle,
His four other companions rushed backwards towards the cover.
While two among those four pretended to pick up the wounded,
The other two followed the first two without any reason.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Getting exhausted, the Mughals beat a retreat from the battlefield, As the (brave) Singhs had taught them a bitter lesson. As the Mughals had accepted their partial defeat, The Nawab was compelled to review his strategy. (24)
lines: Getting exhausted, the Mughals beat a retreat from the battlefield,
As the (brave) Singhs had taught them a bitter lesson.
As the Mughals had accepted their partial defeat,
The Nawab was compelled to review his strategy.

blocks.text: Why should he get his soldiers killed in the battle, When Banda Singh could be starved and made to surrender. Since he had been left with no stocks of food and water inside, Starvation would compell him to ask for a surrender. (25)
lines: Why should he get his soldiers killed in the battle,
When Banda Singh could be starved and made to surrender.
Since he had been left with no stocks of food and water inside,
Starvation would compell him to ask for a surrender.

blocks.text: (So) the Mughals started strengthening their siege around the fort, As they dug a deep channel all around Banda Singh's fort, A few Singhs who used to sneak out of the fort at night, Used to bring some leftovers from garbage for feeding themselves. (26)
lines: (So) the Mughals started strengthening their siege around the fort,
As they dug a deep channel all around Banda Singh's fort,
A few Singhs who used to sneak out of the fort at night,
Used to bring some leftovers from garbage for feeding themselves.

blocks.text: Now with the cutting off of even that meagre supply by the Mughals, The Singhs' plight became extremely vulnerable and miserable, They had to go without food day after day (for a long period), As they had no means of access to any food to feed themselves. (27)
lines: Now with the cutting off of even that meagre supply by the Mughals,
The Singhs' plight became extremely vulnerable and miserable,
They had to go without food day after day (for a long period),
As they had no means of access to any food to feed themselves.

blocks.text: Dohra:

What to talk of food for a minimal nutrition level, Not a grain of food stuff could be procured from anywhere. What to talk of leaves and bark of trees, Even the grass had withered from the bare-earth. (28)
lines: What to talk of food for a minimal nutrition level,
Not a grain of food stuff could be procured from anywhere.
What to talk of leaves and bark of trees,
Even the grass had withered from the bare-earth.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Singhs having found nothing else to feed themselves, Survived for a few days by feeding themselves on clay. Ultimately, the Singhs approached Banda Singh for succour, And shouted near his upper storey dwelling. (29)
lines: The Singhs having found nothing else to feed themselves,
Survived for a few days by feeding themselves on clay.
Ultimately, the Singhs approached Banda Singh for succour,
And shouted near his upper storey dwelling.

blocks.text: They cried that Banda Singh, being divinely Omniscient, Had brought things to such a pass through his own Will. They begged him to have a look at their miserable plight, As hunger and deprivation had drained them completely. (30)
lines: They cried that Banda Singh, being divinely Omniscient,
Had brought things to such a pass through his own Will.
They begged him to have a look at their miserable plight,
As hunger and deprivation had drained them completely.

blocks.text: They suggested him to fly away to a far off place, As they were sure to locate him if they survived this ordeal. Then Banda Singh retorted to them (a bit incensed), That they now wished him to fly away (after such a disaster). (31)
lines: They suggested him to fly away to a far off place,
As they were sure to locate him if they survived this ordeal.
Then Banda Singh retorted to them (a bit incensed),
That they now wished him to fly away (after such a disaster).

blocks.text: He snubbed them for goading him to go back from his promise, For such a petty thing as human life and this material world. Although they had themselves forbidden him to fly away, Now they wished him to turn back from his pledge. (32)
lines: He snubbed them for goading him to go back from his promise,
For such a petty thing as human life and this material world.
Although they had themselves forbidden him to fly away,
Now they wished him to turn back from his pledge.

blocks.text: Dohra:

(These five) a saint, a sati1 and a brave warrior, Together with a learned scholar and an elephant's ivory teeth, Never do they turn back from their stated positions, For ages and ages till the ends of eternity. (33)
lines: (These five) a saint, a sati1 and a brave warrior,
Together with a learned scholar and an elephant's ivory teeth,
Never do they turn back from their stated positions,
For ages and ages till the ends of eternity.

blocks.text: Having taken a solemn pledge (at king Janmeja's2 Yajna), Even the snakes had volunteered to slither into the boiling couldren. How could he (Banda Singh) claim himself to be a great personage, If he now turned back from his pledge (by flying away). (34)
lines: Having taken a solemn pledge (at king Janmeja's2 Yajna),
Even the snakes had volunteered to slither into the boiling couldren.
How could he (Banda Singh) claim himself to be a great personage,
If he now turned back from his pledge (by flying away).

blocks.text: Chaupai:

For keeping his word, the king Balraja3 had to forgo his life as well, And (the Lord of the world) had to become a security guard at Balraja's court. (Similarly) king Harish Chander4 , having made a promise (to Vishwa Mittar), Had to sell himself as a slave at the house of a sweeper. (35)
lines: For keeping his word, the king Balraja3 had to forgo his life as well,
And (the Lord of the world) had to become a security guard at Balraja's court.
(Similarly) king Harish Chander4 , having made a promise (to Vishwa Mittar),
Had to sell himself as a slave at the house of a sweeper.

blocks.text: The Pandavas5 had to stake their wife after making a pledge, Adn had to live in exile (for fourteen years) to keep their pledge. Great men put their lives at stake for keeping their word, And voluntarily accept pain for fulfilling their promise. (36)
lines: The Pandavas5 had to stake their wife after making a pledge,
Adn had to live in exile (for fourteen years) to keep their pledge.
Great men put their lives at stake for keeping their word,
And voluntarily accept pain for fulfilling their promise.

blocks.text: Women burn themselves on their (husband's) funeral pyre, And never hesitate to embrace death to fulfil their oath. An enlisted official (soldier) sacrifices his life for his oath of allegiance), And dies fighting on the battlefield for fulfilling his terms of service. (37)
lines: Women burn themselves on their (husband's) funeral pyre,
And never hesitate to embrace death to fulfil their oath.
An enlisted official (soldier) sacrifices his life for his oath of allegiance),
And dies fighting on the battlefield for fulfilling his terms of service.

blocks.text: An (Indian) daughter leaves for her in-laws house on her father's word, And preserves her family's dignity (at all costs). Guru Teg Bahadur6 , after having made a solemn promise, Sacrificed his life at Delhi to keep his words with the pleading Brahmins. (38)
lines: An (Indian) daughter leaves for her in-laws house on her father's word,
And preserves her family's dignity (at all costs).
Guru Teg Bahadur6 , after having made a solemn promise,
Sacrificed his life at Delhi to keep his words with the pleading Brahmins.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Since Baba Nanak had pronounced his well thought philosophy, It has become mandatory to keep the sanctity of his words. He himself had shed his mortal frame at the age of sixty-nine, Lest he should become senile and incapacitated. (39)
lines: Since Baba Nanak had pronounced his well thought philosophy,
It has become mandatory to keep the sanctity of his words.
He himself had shed his mortal frame at the age of sixty-nine,
Lest he should become senile and incapacitated.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereupon, the Singhs enquired from Banda Singh (about those words), As to what were those injunctions pronounced by Baba Nanak. Banda Singh referred to Guru Nanak's words7 recorded in Guru Granth Sahib, Which implied that every man turned senile at the age of seventy. (40)
lines: Thereupon, the Singhs enquired from Banda Singh (about those words),
As to what were those injunctions pronounced by Baba Nanak.
Banda Singh referred to Guru Nanak's words7 recorded in Guru Granth Sahib,
Which implied that every man turned senile at the age of seventy.

blocks.text: So in case Banda Singh remained alive upto the age of seventy, He would also be counted among the senile and the demented. Then he would feel ashamed to be included in that category, In case he got stigmatised by Baba Nanak's injunction. (41)
lines: So in case Banda Singh remained alive upto the age of seventy,
He would also be counted among the senile and the demented.
Then he would feel ashamed to be included in that category,
In case he got stigmatised by Baba Nanak's injunction.

blocks.text: He would shed his mortal frame to escape that stigma, In order to prove the validity of Baba Nanak's words. If the truth of Baba Nanak's words got violated, Then it would be presumed that the Guru's word in Gurbani, were not true. (42)
lines: He would shed his mortal frame to escape that stigma,
In order to prove the validity of Baba Nanak's words.
If the truth of Baba Nanak's words got violated,
Then it would be presumed that the Guru's word in Gurbani, were not true.

blocks.text: He (Banda Singh) had made a promise to die along with them, And had made a public declaration loud and clear. If he now turned back from his solemn pledge, How would he redeem himself in the Divine Court? (43)
lines: He (Banda Singh) had made a promise to die along with them,
And had made a public declaration loud and clear.
If he now turned back from his solemn pledge,
How would he redeem himself in the Divine Court?
